basis.description:
Identity of what the graph was built from.
`None` only when identity cannot be established at all;
otherwise present with `complete: false` when any component
(workspace canonicalization, manifest digest) is unavailable, or
when the workspace had nothing to analyze.

pending_references.description:
The references the graph could not tie to a declaration.

A file can be read and still state a relation the project cannot
prove: the reference names something nobody declares, or names
several things and the graph cannot tell which one it means.
Those are facts about the code, and they travel with the answer
next to the relations that were resolved.

`Some([])` when every reference was tied. An answer served from
the cache publishes the references of the graph it serves, and a
graph is only persisted when it was built with none of them.

rejected_relationships.description:
The relations the repository refused.

A relation that was refused is not an edge of the graph, and
`relationships_found` counts the relations the graph holds. Naming
the refused ones is what keeps that number and the graph in
agreement.

`Some([])` when every relation was taken. An answer served from
the cache publishes the relations of the graph it serves, and a
graph is only persisted when it was built with none of them.

skipped_files.description:
The holes of the tree, as it is now.
`Some([])` when the walk left nothing out; `Some([..])` when one
or more paths were dropped —because of I/O / parsing failures,
because the walk declined them, or because their language is one
nobody supports yet.

The list belongs to the tree and not to the build that produced
the graph: an answer served from the cache publishes the holes of
the tree as it is NOW, so that no consumer can be told `complete`
about a tree the walk does not read whole.

status.description:
Explicit build outcome surfaced to the caller so
consumers (LLM, CI, alert) can branch on it without parsing
`skipped_files`. Values:
  - `"complete"`: the answer describes the whole tree: no file was
    dropped and no reference was left without a declaration.
  - `"partial"`: something is missing: a file was dropped (I/O or
    parsing failure), a reference could not be tied to a
    declaration, or the repository refused a relation.
  - `"unknown"`: the answer carries no verdict about the coverage
    of the tree.
  - `"unsupported"`: the walk happened and the tree holds no
    source this product can read. Nothing was dropped, but there
    is nothing to be complete about.

The verdict is the tree's, not the build's: an answer served from
the cache says what the tree looks like NOW, which is the same
thing a fresh walk of it would say.

tools.name: safe_refactor
tools.title: Perform safe refactoring with validation and preview
tools.description: Perform safe refactoring with validation and preview.

input_schema.description:
Read-only refactor request.

`deny_unknown_fields` is the AAT-B5-03 guarantee, and it is load-bearing:
this is the *preview* input, the one that crosses the read-only MCP
boundary, and `apply` takes its `AuthorizationToken` over a separate
channel. Without it, serde silently drops an `authorization_token` field
a caller sent — the preview would accept a write-authority field and
ignore it, and the caller would believe it had done something.

The test that pins this (`b5_w3_apply_with_authority::
read_only_mcp_tool_cannot_acquire_write_authority`) was written before the
attribute was here. It never reported the gap because it lives in
`core-unrestricted-evidence-kernel`, which had never completed a run.

limitations: preview by default; --apply required to mutate

tools.name: safe_refactor_preview
tools.title: Render a deterministic preview of a RefactorPlan without mutating files
tools.description: Read a RefactorPlan (B5.W1) from a plan file or a JSON string and produce a RefactorPreview (B5.W2): per-file unified diff, original vs new bytes, workspace state digest, and preconditions/risks summary. The function is pure: same plan + same bytes => byte-equal preview, and it NEVER mutates the workspace. B5.W3 (apply) reuses the workspace_state_digest to detect concurrent modifications between preview and apply.

input_schema.description:
`safe_refactor_preview` input, in the shape the catalogue publishes.

`plan_path` and `plan_json` are alternatives (the catalogue's `oneOf`), so
exactly one has to arrive. Resolving which one is a precondition, not a
default: silently preferring one would mean a caller who sent the other got
a preview of the wrong thing.

plan_path.description: Absolute path to a RefactorPlan JSON file.

limitations: preview only; apply requires explicit authorization (B5.W3)

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.title: Explain why a finding is reported
tools.description: Explain why a finding is reported. Takes the path of a source file; the findings pipeline runs over that file and the answer names each finding's kind, severity, status, message, causal chain and detector, and states whether the grounding behind it could be verified. A file with no findings says so instead of returning an empty list.

finding_id.description:
Only explain this finding.

Absent means "every finding the pipeline reports for the file". The
ids the answer publishes are the ones to ask about.

path.description:
The source file whose findings are explained.

Relative to the workspace root, or absolute inside it. The path is
validated before it is read: a path that leaves the workspace is
refused, and a path that cannot be read is an error, not an empty
answer.

coverage.description:
Lo que la respuesta cubre del árbol que se midió.

`None` cuando la respuesta no dice nada de la cobertura: nadie la
midió.

freshness.description:
Sobre qué árbol y qué instantánea se calculó.

`None` cuando la respuesta no lo declara.

lsp_confirmed_edges.description:
Las aristas que un LSP confirmó.

`None` siempre, hoy: el producto no publica un recuento de aristas
confirmadas por LSP, y un `0` sería una medición que nadie hizo.

Budget.description: Lo que la respuesta dejó fuera.

omitted.description: Cuántos elementos quedaron fuera, cuando la respuesta lo dice.

page.description: El handle firmado por el que se sigue leyendo.

reason.description: Por qué quedaron fuera, cuando la respuesta lo dice.

CausalStepExplanation.description: One step of a finding's causal chain.

detail.description: The human-readable detail of the step.

evidence.description: The evidence handle the step rests on, when it rests on one.

fact.description: The canonical fact the step rests on, when it rests on one.

kind.description: The role the step plays in the explanation.

subject.description: The entity the step concerns, when it names one.

pending_references.description: Las referencias que no se pudieron atar a una declaración.

rejected_relationships.description: Las relaciones que el repositorio rechazó.

skipped_files.description: Los ficheros que la lectura no pudo leer.

status.description:
El veredicto de la cobertura: `complete`, `partial`, `unknown` o
`unsupported`.

DetectorExplanation.description: The detector as it was executed.

authority.description: The authority the detector held when it produced the finding.

instance_digest.description: The digest of the whole definition.

logic_digest.description: The digest of the detector's logic.

policy_digest.description: The digest of the detector's finding policy.

semantic_digest.description: The digest of logic and policy together.

version.description: The detector's version at production time.

oneOf.description: The pipeline reported the finding(s) and the answer explains them.
The pipeline ran over the file and reported nothing.

The pipeline ran and reported findings, but not the one that was
asked for.

constructs_grounded.description: Constructs whose canonical fact was resolved.

constructs_ungrounded.description: Constructs with no canonical fact, or with an ambiguous one.

FindingExplanation.description: One finding, with the reason it is reported.

detector.description: The detector as it was executed.

evidence_class.description: The strength of the supporting evidence.

gateable.description: Whether the finding may block the gate.

id.description: The finding's id, as the pipeline minted it.

message.description: The human-readable message the detector produced.

graph_source.description: De dónde salió el grafo: `built`, `cache` o `daemon`.

snapshot.description:
El digest del manifiesto de fuentes: el mismo árbol da el mismo
digest, y cualquier cambio lo cambia.

workspace.description: El workspace canónico del que se calculó.

evidence.description: The evidence handles the finding claims.

facts.description: The canonical facts the causal chain rests on.

reason.description: Why the grounding could not be verified, when it could not.

verified.description:
Whether the grounding could be verified: the evidence resolves and
the causal chain agrees with it.

`false` with an empty evidence list means the finding claims nothing;
`false` with a reason means it claims something that could not be
resolved. The two are not the same, and the reason says which.

authority.description: La autoridad de la tool: `read`, `mutating`, `execute` o `network`.

handle.description: El handle firmado que el enlace lleva, cuando lo lleva.

precondition.description: Lo que tiene que ser verdad antes de llamar a la tool.

reason.description: Por qué existe este enlace.

rel.description:
Qué clase de enlace es: `resolve-ambiguity`, `continue`,
`inspect-callers`, `reindex`, `inspect-risk` o `preview-change`.

required_args.description: Los argumentos con los que hay que llamarla.

tool.description: La tool que responde al enlace.

output_schema.description: La respuesta, con lo que la sostiene y lo que viene después.

_links.description: Lo que se puede hacer ahora.

basis.description: Sobre qué se apoya la respuesta.

budget.description: Lo que la respuesta dejó fuera.

coverage.description: What the run looked at, and what it could establish.

findings.description:
The findings, each with its reason.

Empty when `outcome` is `NoFindings` or `NotReported` — and in those
cases the outcome says which of the two it is, so an empty list is
never the whole answer.

path.description: The file the answer is about, as it was asked for.

summary.description: One line saying what the answer says.

schema_version.description: La versión de la forma del sobre.

El veredicto de la respuesta: `complete`, `partial`, `unknown`,
`unsupported` o `failed`.

La palabra la declara quien midió; el sobre no la inventa.
